Architecture and Module Surface

This page collects the real sla_ecs module names extracted from sa_plugin_sla regression and macro-analysis documents, and the expansion shapes of the TableErased query-combination family. After reading it you will be able to match the file names that recur in regression records and understand what each of them is responsible for.

Notesla_ecs has 54 lib modules (as of 2026-07-01); the table below only lists files that actually appear in the help materials, not a complete list; the “Role” column is each document’s description of its usage, not the library’s own API documentation.

Real Module Names under lib

ModuleRole in the documents
lib/world_table_erased.slaThe largest table-erased world definition, the main body of the TableErased combination family; the reproduction file for the frontend check crash in the Module Table retest. As of 2026-07-19: about 678KB / 571 functions after expansion.
lib/system_param_table_erased.slaThe file containing the system-param runner family; contains generated functions such as table_erased_run_any_of$N_query_resource_system.
lib/parallel_table_erased.slaTable-erased parallel runners (readonly/mut); the reproduction file for the default SAB path panic 8701.
lib/parallel_iterator.slaParallel iterator (chunk splitting, thread closure); the reproduction file for the strict SAB PhiStateConflict.
lib/parallel_runner.slaOne of the parallel runner entry points; a 2026-07-19 record gives its check transitive ordered module count as ordered modules=16.
lib/parallel.slaThe host regression target designated by the compiler workspace rules.
lib/task_pool_builder.slaTask pool building; the EcsParallelTaskPool configuration struct appears in compiler fix records.
lib/task_scope_completion.slaScope completion (finishing pending tasks); the downstream reproduction file for issue038.
lib/entity_set.slaCited in the macro analysis document: manually implements value-type helpers such as entity_hash.
lib/table_erased_access.sla, lib/schedule_table_erased.slaSample modules for the before/after getOrParse timing comparison of the 2026-07-19 type-scan cache optimization.
lib/schedule_stepping.sla, lib/parallel_mut_writeback.sla, lib/entity_dynamic.slaOther lib modules that appear as downstream verification targets in compiler progress records.

The TableErased Query-Combination Family

The variable-length expansion driven by @expand_tuple covers the main shapes of query combinations. The table below records the ranges and generated counts from the macro-gap analysis document (v0.1 / 2026-07-01):

Expansion kindRangeGenerated count
TableErasedAnyOf$N structs2..87 structs
TableErasedWithAnyOf$N structs2..87 structs
TableErasedPairWithAnyOf$N structs2..87 structs
TableErasedCombination$N structs2..1615 structs
table_erased_query_combinations$N functions2..1615 functions
table_erased_query_pair_mut_combinations$N functions2..1615 functions
table_erased_world_query_any_of$N functions2..87 × 3 world paths
table_erased_world_query_with_any_of$N functions2..87 × 3 world paths
table_erased_world_query_pair_with_any_of$N functions2..87 × 3 world paths
NoteThese ranges are not fixed. The AnyOf9 retest record (discovered 2026-07-06, fixed/verified 2026-07-19) records: world_table_erased.sla expanded the generation range of the direct TableErasedAnyOf / table_erased_world_query_any_of$N from AnyOf5..8 to AnyOf5..9; system_param_table_erased.sla expanded table_erased_run_any_of$N_query_resource_system to AnyOf9, and likewise expanded the direct AnyOf and nested WithAnyOf/PairWithAnyOf runners of the relationship / observer wrappers to AnyOf9. When citing a concrete range, note the date of the basis.

Three Categories of system-param Runners

system-param combination runners are divided by world path into three categories: ordinary / observer / relationship. The scale given by the macro-gap analysis is “7 functions × 3 world paths × 3 categories” (range 2..8); the same document, when discussing combination generation, also describes these three paths as the ordinary/observer/relationship paths. These functions are not a Cartesian product of parameter types that an arity template can directly express — each runner is a combination of 1–5 base parameters (such as Query, Commands, ResMut, MessageReader, MessageWriter), multiplied by three world variants, thus forming hundreds of hand-written functions (the document estimates 300+).

This also explains why the code volume at this layer puts the greatest pressure on the compiler’s import expansion and reachability analysis: most of the timing samples in Known Issues and Regression History come from these few files.
